rule: In the side view the eye stays inside the front quarter section of the head, drawn as a small wedge set back from the front.
Divide nose-to-chin into thirds; the mouth sits about one third down from the nose.
Eyes are typically one eye width apart.
Stretching the jaw and lower face down ages a character; moving it up makes the character younger.
Avoid drawing every tooth; hint at the teeth as a shape.
Squash and stretch keep the volume: a stretched part becomes thinner, a squashed part wider.
